questions.prompt: What is a product in a chemical reaction?
options: A new substance created by the reaction
The starting material before the reaction
The energy the reaction gives off
questions.explanation: A product is a new substance that the reaction creates from the reactants.
questions.misconception: The starting material is the reactant, and energy is not a product in this sense — the product is the new substance formed on the right.

questions.prompt: Where are products written in a chemical equation?
options: On the RIGHT side of the arrow
On the LEFT side of the arrow
In the middle of the arrow
questions.explanation: Products are always written on the right of the arrow; reactants are on the left.
questions.misconception: The left side belongs to reactants — the right side is where the products appear.

questions.prompt: Where do a product's atoms come from?
options: Exactly from the reactants — they are rearranged, not new
From the air around the reaction
They are created fresh during the reaction
From the energy of the reaction
questions.explanation: A product's atoms are exactly the reactant atoms, reconnected — nothing is created or destroyed.
questions.misconception: Atoms are never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction — the product simply rearranges the atoms the reactants already had.

questions.prompt: How does the mass of the products compare to the mass of the reactants?
options: They are equal — atoms are conserved
questions.explanation: Since the product atoms are exactly the reactant atoms, the total mass never changes — conservation of mass.
questions.misconception: Products never lose or gain atoms, so they can never weigh more or less — the mass is always equal on both sides.
